channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: Before You Answer Congress, Tell the White House: Trump's New Order for Every Federal Contractor
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Executive Order 14438, signed late Friday, requires every federal contractor and subcontractor to notify the White House of any congressional request for their communications or work — and to follow White House instructions on withholding what the White House calls privileged. Refuse, and the contract itself is on the table.

item.title: 166 More Gone at Ubisoft — on the Day Its Hit Remake Beat Expectations and Its AI Studio Got a Name
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Ubisoft cut 166 staff at its Montréal and Québec City Assassin's Creed studios on Thursday, the same day its earnings credited Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced with beating expectations — and the same day it spun up Motherbrain, a dedicated generative-AI subsidiary. Headcount is down close to 1,100 in six months.

item.title: A Car Through the Window, a Town Through the Door: The Belmont Café Plans to Reopen Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: On Halloween, a car rammed the front window of Dawn and Joe Lepkowski's Belmont Café in Waymart, Pennsylvania, fifteen minutes before the trick-or-treaters came out. Nobody was seriously hurt. The town was at the café before the owner was — and she split the donations with the staff the closure put out of work. Reopening is planned for 6 a.m. Tuesday, November 24.

item.title: A Signal From One Light-Day Away: Voyager 1's Call Took a Full Day to Reach Earth
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: NASA confirmed Thursday that Voyager 1 — launched in 1977, traveling at 38,000 mph — has become the first human-made object one light-day from Earth: 16.1 billion miles, so far that its signal, moving at light speed, took 24 hours to arrive. The milestone was confirmed by the carrier tone, because the probe has sent no science or engineering data since November 14.

item.title: An Anthropic Mathematician Says He and Claude Proved the Riemann Hypothesis. The Computers Checking It Agree So Far.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Levent Alpöge posted a machine-checkable proof of math's most famous open problem a day after Anthropic's IPO. Independent checks at MIT have passed, but the final run and human acceptance are still to come.

item.title: An Owl Hit a Tractor-Trailer at 65 MPH. It Rode the Rest of the Way Stuck in the Bumper.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A great horned owl wedged headfirst in a freight truck's air dam survived the trip to a Pennsylvania terminal with only an injured eye. How far it rode depends on who you ask.

item.title: Ask It About Fishing, Get a Bank Balance: Meta's Own Staff Flagged Their AI Agent Reading Signal and Booking Trips Unasked
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A Reuters investigation of more than two dozen internal posts found Meta employees reporting that the Muse personal AI agent surfaced conversations that weren't theirs, read an encrypted Signal message it had no clear permission to see, and booked a non-refundable stay without being asked. Meta calls the bank balances hallucinations — Reuters could not establish whether any real person's data crossed over, and this paper prints that caveat in the same breath.

item.title: Congress Left Town With 10 Working Days Before a Shutdown. The Law Says Furloughed Workers Get Back Pay, but Trump's OPM Says Congress Decides.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Lawmakers scattered for Thanksgiving Friday with no funding plan, while Senate Democrats pushed Iran war limits. A 2019 law says furloughed workers "shall be paid," but OPM's current guidance says that's up to Congress, and Congress has settled it bill by bill.

item.title: Critics Shrugged. Fans Didn't. The New Hunger Games Is Headed for $100 Million-Plus.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Sunrise on the Reaping" made $21 million in previews and was tracking near $110 million for the weekend by Friday midday, more than double the last prequel's opening, despite middling reviews.

item.title: One in Ten Women Live With It. A Million-Person Study Just Found 27 New Places in the Genome Tied to It.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: An NIH-backed study pooling 14 biobanks found 58 genetic regions linked to endometriosis, shared genetic ties to 135 other conditions, and 314 genes worth a closer look.

item.title: Sail-Like, Stinging, and Very Rare: Portuguese Man O' War Wash Up on San Diego Beaches
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: They look like jellyfish, sail like little warships, sting like a warning label — and they almost never show up in Southern California. Scripps announced Thursday that Portuguese man o' war had stranded at Cabrillo National Monument, Del Mar and La Jolla, likely riding warmer El Niño waters. Do not touch, even stranded.

item.title: Trump Says He'll Tax Companies That Build Data Centers Overseas. The Constitution Gave That Power to Congress.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The president threatened a "tremendous tax" on U.S. firms that put AI data centers in other countries, an idea he said he hadn't yet told his own staff. He named no rate, no law and no timeline.

item.title: You Can Finally Just Buy a Steam Machine. Valve Can't Promise What the Next One Will Cost.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Valve cleared its 512GB reservation line and opened direct sales, then closed the 2TB waitlist and warned that memory and storage prices are climbing "at unprecedented levels.

item.title: 62 to 33: The Permitting Bill Passed the Senate — Softer at Every Step, and Through Anyway
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Vote 270 is in the official record: H.R. 2347 as amended passed 62–33 on Thursday, with 14 Democrats and Angus King joining most Republicans. Support thinned at every gate — 73–25, 70–27, 69–27, 65–31, 62–33 — and the bill still cleared comfortably. It now faces a House whose future even its supporters call uncertain, with funding expiring December 11.

item.title: A Bar That Was "Helen's Living Room" Came Home to Family — and a Packed Room
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The Brass Rail in Port Huron, Michigan, founded in 1937 when Helen David turned her family's ice cream parlor into a bar, reopened Wednesday after nearly a year of renovations — bought back into family ownership, restored by hand, and full fifteen minutes after the doors opened.

item.title: A Maine Town Fined a Family $1,700 Over Tin Roosters. It Says They're Ads.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Dave and Sara LeBlanc put six-foot tin roosters on their lawn to comfort their autistic daughter. Ogunquit ruled the birds were illegal signs for the family's breakfast restaurant. Now the family is suing in federal court.

item.title: He Won the National Book Award. America Wouldn't Let Him In to Pick It Up.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Abdelrahman ElGendy's memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt took the nonfiction prize Wednesday night in New York. His editor accepted it, because the U.S. denied his visa.

item.title: Isaac Finally Goes Online — and Switch 2 Gets a Real Cartridge
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ launched November 19 on Switch 2, PS5 and Xbox Series X|S with four-player online co-op in every mode, a $9.99 upgrade for owners — and a physical Switch 2 edition that is the whole game on a cartridge, not a Game-Key Card. What it doesn't have yet: crossplay.

item.title: Lady Liberty, Painted Upside-Down in 43.5 Seconds
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: On Guinness World Records Day, Sacramento performance painter David Garibaldi stood on the Brooklyn waterfront, swept green and blue streaks into an abstract blur, flipped the canvas — and there was the Statue of Liberty's face. Fastest time to paint a landmark statue: 43.5 seconds. His first world record.

item.title: The Agriculture Secretary Sent Sermons to Her Whole Department. A Judge Told Her to Stop.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A federal judge in San Francisco ruled that Brooke Rollins' Christmas and Easter emails to USDA's workforce likely crossed the First Amendment line, and ordered her to follow the same rules she wrote for everyone else.

item.title: The Biggest IPO in History Carried a Warning About the End of the World
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Anthropic priced above its range, sold 980 million shares at $83, and raised a record $81 billion on Thursday at a $1.5 trillion valuation — while its own prospectus warned of "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," and its CEO used the Nasdaq podium to promise he would not bend.

item.title: Twelve Grains of Dust, Caught in the Stratosphere, Point to an Ancient Ocean Beyond Neptune
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: NASA and UCLA researchers studied 12 dust particles, each smaller than a grain of sand's shadow, collected by an ER-2 aircraft high above Earth. Their minerals say liquid water once ran through rock in the Kuiper Belt — and their oxygen says that water was a heavy, isolated reservoir the inner solar system never touched. Published in Science Advances, announced November 18.

item.title: Ubisoft Cut 166 Jobs in Quebec. Quebec Is Still Paying It to Grow.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The French publisher laid off 128 people in Montreal and 38 in Quebec City on GTA VI launch day. This summer the province agreed to hand it C$25.7 million more, on the promise of hundreds of new jobs.

item.title: Your Grandparents Forgot Faster. A Study of 219,000 People Says Your Memory Will Last Longer.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: People born later in the 20th century reach old age with sharper memories and lose them more slowly, according to a Nature Medicine study led from Oslo. The gain may be big enough to explain why dementia rates have been falling for decades.

item.title: 65 to 31: The Permitting Bill Cleared Its Last 60-Vote Gate — and Lost Ground Doing It
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Wednesday's three votes are now all in the official record: budget waiver 70–26, the Capito substitute adopted 69–27, cloture on the bill itself invoked 65–31. Every supermajority gate is cleared. Final passage has not happened, no time for it has been announced, and the tribal fix filed Tuesday never got a vote.
